Hugo Grotius was a Dutch lawyer and scholar, born in Delft in 1583, who is seen as one of the founders of international law.

Writing for the Dutch East India Company, he argued in The Free Sea of 1609 that the oceans belong to no one and are open to all nations, against the Portuguese and Spanish claims. His great book On the Law of War and Peace of 1625 set out rules that should bind states even in war, based on natural law rather than religion alone.

In the religious quarrels of the Dutch Republic he was sentenced to life in prison in 1619, but escaped in 1621 hidden in a book chest. He lived in exile and served Sweden as ambassador in Paris. His ideas shaped the law of nations after the Thirty Years' War and later the United Nations. See the Netherlands.
sum: Hugo Grotius was a Dutch lawyer and scholar, born in Delft in 1583, who is seen as one of the founders of international law.
